original_recommendation.title: Resolve KPI and product mismatch in campaign setup
original_recommendation.whats_happening: The campaign primary goal references credit card signups while the offering is recorded as Personal Loans, creating a tracking and KPI alignment risk.
what_you_should_do: Audit the campaign naming, goal text, and conversion actions in Google Ads and your reporting dashboards to identify where 'credit card' vs 'personal loans' labels are used.
Update campaign objective and conversion action names so they explicitly match the actual product you want to measure (e.g., 'Personal Loan - Lead' or 'Credit Card - Signup').
If multiple products are advertised, create distinct campaigns or conversion actions per product to avoid cross-attribution.
original_recommendation.why_this_matters: If conversions are being tracked for the wrong product, ROAS, CPA and lead counts will not reflect the intended business outcome and budget decisions will be based on misleading data.
original_recommendation.expected_impact: Restores measurement accuracy so reported ROAS and CPA reflect the right product and supports correct budget and optimization decisions.

original_recommendation.title: Tie conversions to downstream value (quality, conversion-to-customer and LTV)
original_recommendation.whats_happening: Revenue and ROAS are reported but there is no linkage to customer lifetime value, margins, or lead-to-customer conversion rates.
what_you_should_do: Connect Google Ads conversion IDs to CRM records so you can measure lead-to-funder (or customer) conversion rates and revenue over time.
Track post-conversion events (approval, funded loan, charged-off status) and calculate LTV or contribution margin for cohorts originating from this campaign.
Use those downstream metrics to set target CPA or target ROAS that reflect business profitability rather than short-term attributed revenue.
original_recommendation.why_this_matters: ROAS >1 alone does not guarantee profitability. Connecting to LTV and downstream outcomes allows deciding whether current CPA and ROAS meet business profitability thresholds.
original_recommendation.expected_impact: Improves decision-making on budget, bidding, and allowable CPA by aligning acquisition metrics with real customer value.

original_recommendation.title: Enable reach and audience saturation metrics
original_recommendation.whats_happening: Reach is null in the data, preventing assessment of audience saturation and frequency for the campaign.
what_you_should_do: Activate reach and frequency reporting where available in Google Ads and track unique reach and impressions per audience cohort.
Segment performance by audience (new users vs returning, in-market segments) to detect saturation or diminishing returns.
Apply frequency caps or rotate creative if you identify high frequency with declining CTR or conversion rate.
original_recommendation.why_this_matters: Knowing reach and frequency helps balance prospecting and remarketing, avoid audience fatigue, and optimize where additional spend will drive incremental conversions.
original_recommendation.expected_impact: Improved audience management, reduced wasted impressions from overexposure, and better allocation between prospecting and remarketing.

original_recommendation.title: Populate lead count and cost-per-lead (CPL) in reporting
original_recommendation.whats_happening: Fields for 'leads' and 'cpl' are null, so lead-level efficiency cannot be evaluated despite having conversions and CPA.
what_you_should_do: Confirm the definition of a 'lead' and ensure the conversion action representing a lead is firing on the site or funnel.
Add a CPL metric to the reporting pipeline (CPL = Spend / Leads) and backfill if possible for recent reporting windows.
Validate tracking by creating test leads and confirming they appear in Google Ads and your reports, then monitor leads and CPL daily until stable.
original_recommendation.why_this_matters: Lead counts and CPL are primary KPIs for a leads objective. Without them you cannot verify that conversions represent qualifying leads or compare performance to target CPL.
original_recommendation.expected_impact: Enables direct comparison of campaign performance to lead-level targets and prevents misinterpretation of conversion data.

original_recommendation.title: Address single-channel dependency by testing alternative channels
original_recommendation.whats_happening: Only Google Search data is present, creating risk of over-dependence on a single channel for leads and revenue.
what_you_should_do: Run small, controlled tests (pilot budgets) on at least one other channel (e.g., display, social, or performance networks) to compare CPA and ROAS.
Measure cost per conversion and attributed revenue consistently across channels using the same conversion definitions.
If alternatives show comparable or better efficiency, reallocate a portion of budget away from single-channel concentration.
original_recommendation.why_this_matters: Relying solely on one channel increases exposure to platform-specific volatility and misses opportunities to find cheaper or higher-quality leads.
original_recommendation.expected_impact: Reduces risk of performance volatility and may lower average CPA or improve ROAS by finding more efficient channels.

original_recommendation.title: Scale search investment cautiously given positive ROAS and low CPA
original_recommendation.whats_happening: Campaign shows ROAS of 1.8 and a CPA of $16.74 with a 7.5% conversion rate, indicating conversion efficiency that could allow scaled spend.
what_you_should_do: Run a controlled scale test: increase daily budget by a fixed percentage (e.g., 20–30%) for a short test window and monitor CPA and ROAS closely.
Prefer incremental scaling across top-performing keywords and audiences rather than across the entire campaign.
Use experiments or drafts in Google Ads to test bidding or budget changes and set clear stop rules if CPA or ROAS deteriorates.
original_recommendation.why_this_matters: If the observed efficiency holds when scaled, increasing budget can increase volume of leads and revenue; if it worsens, controlled testing limits wasted spend.
original_recommendation.expected_impact: Potential increase in lead volume and attributed revenue while containing downside risk through controlled experiments.

original_recommendation.title: Improve attribution and cross-channel reporting setup
original_recommendation.whats_happening: Analysis likely relies on single-channel (last-click) attribution and lacks cross-channel credit, limiting understanding of true channel contribution.
what_you_should_do: Enable auto-tagging and ensure conversion import and first-party data flows are configured correctly between Google Ads and analytics/CRM.
Consider a data-driven attribution model or a simple multi-touch model in Google Ads to better reflect assisted conversions.
Build a unified dashboard that ingests cost and conversion data from other channels so comparisons use consistent definitions.
original_recommendation.why_this_matters: Better attribution reduces the chance of over-investing in channels that appear strong under last-click and under-investing in channels that assist conversions.
original_recommendation.expected_impact: More accurate channel-level performance insights and improved budget allocation across channels.
